benchmark_name: Step 1 + Step 2A: External Human Washout (PMID 38393578), Live openFDA FAERS (21.05M Reports) & OpenCYP-FTQC v1.2 Entanglement (CAS 13e,13o / 2.94M Determinants)

epistemic_demarcation.clinical_claim_boundary: Strictly non-commercial research shadow-mode validation under NHS DCB0129/DCB0160; FAERS disproportionality reflects spontaneous reporting associations, not causal incidence, and Day 7 (+48h) intracellular ritonavir retention residual keeps H-LTC-02 strictly OPEN.

openfda_database_metadata.regulatory_disclaimer: Do not rely on openFDA to make decisions regarding medical care. Always speak to your health provider about the risks and benefits of FDA-regulated products.

trial_metadata.perpetrator_regimen: Oral ritonavir 100 mg twice daily on Days 1-5 (discontinued after Day 5)
trial_metadata.probe_substrate: Oral microdosed midazolam 25 ug (CYP3A4 index substrate)

pubmed_clinical_concordance_register.title: Time Course of the Interaction Between Oral Short-Term Ritonavir Therapy with Three Factor Xa Inhibitors and the Activity of CYP2D6, CYP2C19, and CYP3A4 in Healthy Volunteers.
pubmed_clinical_concordance_register.clinical_role_in_cqwm: Primary 8-visit out-of-sample human 5-day ritonavir (100 mg BID) + midazolam washout benchmark (Day 7 +48h AUCR 10.2x, Day 9 +96h AUCR 2.91x, CYP3A4 recovery t1/2 = 2.30 +/- 0.89 d).

pubmed_clinical_concordance_register.title: Determining the time course of CYP3A inhibition by potent reversible and irreversible CYP3A inhibitors using A limited sampling strategy.
pubmed_clinical_concordance_register.clinical_role_in_cqwm: Direct human head-to-head contrast proving reversible voriconazole recovers within 24 h while irreversible MBI ritonavir requires multi-day enzyme resynthesis.

pubmed_clinical_concordance_register.title: The contribution of intestinal and hepatic CYP3A to the interaction between midazolam and clarithromycin.
pubmed_clinical_concordance_register.clinical_role_in_cqwm: Seminal human IV + oral midazolam crossover dissecting intestinal vs hepatic CYP3A inactivation under clarithromycin (oral AUCR ~7-8x vs IV ~3.2x).

pubmed_clinical_concordance_register.title: Interaction between midazolam and clarithromycin in the elderly.
pubmed_clinical_concordance_register.clinical_role_in_cqwm: Prospective elderly human crossover confirming persistent ~8.0x oral midazolam AUCR surge under clarithromycin 500 mg BID.

pubmed_clinical_concordance_register.title: Inhibition of human intestinal wall metabolism by macrolide antibiotics: effect of clarithromycin on cytochrome P450 3A4/5 activity and expression.
pubmed_clinical_concordance_register.clinical_role_in_cqwm: Paired human small-bowel endoscopic biopsies demonstrating >70% loss of catalytic CYP3A4 activity without mRNA/protein loss (direct proof of nitroso-alkane MIC).

pubmed_clinical_concordance_register.title: Rate of onset of inhibition of gut-wall and hepatic CYP3A by clarithromycin.
pubmed_clinical_concordance_register.clinical_role_in_cqwm: Time-course human intestinal biopsy + midazolam study showing rapid 64% Dose-1 enterocyte CYP3A inactivation followed by delayed hepatic MBI.

pubmed_clinical_concordance_register.title: Effects of paroxetine on the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of immediate-release and extended-release metoprolol.
pubmed_clinical_concordance_register.clinical_role_in_cqwm: Human 3-way crossover demonstrating 3-4x S/R-metoprolol AUC elevation and beta-blockade surge from paroxetine CYP2D6 MBI (`CQWM-05`).
